reasoning: Artemis II is scheduled for February 2026, just before the forecast date of March 6, 2026, meaning the mission would likely be in progress or recently completed. Historical spaceflight safety data shows modern NASA missions have excellent safety records. Artemis I (uncrewed) succeeded in 2022. While deep space missions involve higher radiation exposure and greater distances than ISS operations, the Orion capsule includes redundant safety systems and a free-return trajectory design. Recent concerns about life support and heat shield damage were investigated before launch. Given NASA's safety protocols, the mission's design redundancies, and the historical rarity of lethal spaceflight disasters in modern era (last US crewed spaceflight fatality was 2003 Columbia), the probability of a lethal outcome is low but non-negligible given the mission's inherent risks.
